title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards for API design, coding, infrastructure, model serving, observability, and performance. It also summarizes the canonical decision records (ADRs) that inform these standards and provides recommended operational runbooks for adoption. Use this as the reference for new services, major refactors, and model onboarding work.

Scope

- API standards (REST/HTTP, error handling, versioning, pagination, rate limiting, auth)
- Coding standards (language-specific guidelines, linting, testing, CI/CD gates)
- Infrastructure standards (accounts, networking, IaC, secrets, capacity)
- Model-serving standards (model packaging, quantization profiles, KV cache, fallback variants)
- Observability standards (metrics, traces, logs, dashboards, alerting)
- Performance standards (SLOs, benchmarking, perf regression process)
- ADR catalog (summary of key architectural decisions and owners)

Executive summary

Redwood's platform must be reliable, cost-efficient, and predictable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. These standards balance developer velocity with operational safety: define minimal required controls (auth, SLOs, rollout policies), measurable signals (metrics + dashboards), and prescriptive procedures for high-risk changes (model rollout, infra changes).

1) API standards

Goals: predictable client experience, forward-compatible changes, clear observability and error semantics.

Requirements:

- Surface: All public/internal endpoints must use REST/JSON (prefer application/json; support streaming via server-sent events or HTTP chunked for long outputs).
- Versioning: Use path-versioning (/v1/...) for breaking changes. Backwards compatible changes can use additive fields.
- Authentication: OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens for internal services; API keys for external clients. All tokens validated via central auth gateway.
- Error model: Use HTTP status codes per RFC; error body MUST be {"code": string, "message": string, "details": optional array} Example:

  {
    "code": "quota_exceeded",
    "message": "Monthly quota exceeded for project 12345"
  }

- Pagination: Cursor-based pagination for lists (>100 items). Include top-level "next_cursor" and "limit" fields.
- Rate limiting: Services expose X-RateLimit-* headers and return 429 with a Retry-After. Gateway enforces per-API quotas.
- Contract & discovery: Maintain OpenAPI spec in service repo (openapi.yaml). CI validates that generated clients match spec.

API Design Checklist (required for PRs):

1. OpenAPI spec added/updated and validated in CI.
2. Auth rules defined and audited.
3. Backwards-compatibility review completed.
4. End-to-end integration test that asserts error shapes and paging.

2) Coding standards

Overview: Encourage consistency and maintainability across Go, Python, and TypeScript services.

General rules:

- Style & formatting: Enforce gofmt/golines for Go, black/isort/ruff for Python, prettier/eslint for TypeScript. CI must fail on formatting violations.
- Linting: All repos must include static analysis; critical lint errors must block merges.
- Tests: Target minimum 80% coverage for core runtime logic; for infra and orchestration code, focus on integration and contract tests.
- Type safety: Use typed interfaces (Go, TypeScript) and mypy/pyright for Python where feasible.
- Dependency management: Pin dependencies with automated updates via Dependabot or Renovate. Vulnerable dependencies must be remediated within 7 days for critical CVEs.

3) Infrastructure standards

Goals: secure, reproducible, and observable infra changes across cloud accounts and private deployments.

Account & network:
- Use centralized cloud accounts organized by environment: prod, staging, dev, sandbox.
- VPC layout: per-customer private deployments use dedicated VPCs and subnets; hosted services isolate control plane in dedicated management VPCs.

IaC & change control:
- All infra changes via Terraform modules in the mono-repo (or designated infra repos).
- PRs must include plan output and security review for changes to IAM, network, or KMS.
- State: Remote state stored in secured backend with ACLs and encryption (e.g., S3 + Dynamo/StateLock).

Secrets & keys:
- Use cloud KMS/HSM for production key material. Secrets stored in Vault with RBAC and audit logging. Short-lived credentials are preferred.

Capacity & scaling:
- Reserved capacity services declare capacity targets and autoscaling policies in a capacity manifest (example table in Appendix A).

Appendix A: Example capacity manifest table (CSV style)

- service_name, target_rps, target_p95_latency_ms, buffer_margin_percent
- inference-hosted, 2000, 250, 20
- inference-dedicated, 5000, 120, 25

4) Model-serving standards

Packaging & verification:
- Models are packaged with metadata.json containing: model_id, architecture, parameters, tokenizer_version, quantization_profile_id, expected_memory_mb, peak_vram_mb.
- Each model must have a verified performance profile (benchmark suite) stored in bench-results/ in the model repo. Bench results include throughput (tokens/sec), p50/p95 latency at target batch sizes, and memory usage.

Quantization & variants:
- Standard quantization profiles (A, B, C) maintained in /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Profiles specify target accuracy degradation (<2% allowed for recommended profiles) and hardware compatibility.
- Service must support automatic fallback to a higher-accuracy variant when quality gates fail.

KV cache & batching:
- KV cache warming policy: warm on canary traffic for new versions. Cache keys must include model_id, model_version, prompt_prefix_hash.
- Batching: Continuous batching is enabled with latency caps per route. Batching parameters (max_batch_size, max_wait_ms) declared in service config.

Rollout policy (model):

1. Canary 1% traffic for 24 hours with synthetic and real traffic tests.
2. Validate key metrics: p95 latency, error rate, quality metrics on held-out prompt set.
3. Gradual ramp (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on SLO violations or quality regressions.

5) Observability standards

Signals to emit (minimum):

- Metrics: request_count, request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), error_count (by code), token_generation_count, batch_size_distribution, cache_hit_rate. Metrics must include labels: service, route, model_id, model_version, region, env.
- Tracing: Distributed tracing with 100% sampling on errors and 1% baseline sampling otherwise. Span naming must include route and model_version.
- Logs: Structured JSON logs with request_id, timestamp, level, message, and key context (customer_id, model_id). PII must never be logged.

Dashboards & alerts:
- Per-service dashboard with latency percentiles, 5xx rate, token cost breakdown, and model quality regressions.
- Alert rules (examples):
  - page when p95 latency > target for 5m AND error_rate > 0.5% (pagerduty)
  - slack notify when cache_hit_rate drops > 10% relative to baseline (SRE channel)

6) Performance standards and benchmarking

SLOs (example defaults):
- Inference-hosted public API: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for short responses (<64 tokens), error rate <0.5%, availability 99.9% monthly.
- Dedicated inference pool: p95 latency <= 150ms (target workload), availability 99.95%.

Benchmarking requirements:
- Every model onboarding must include: synthetic microbench (latency vs batch size), end-to-end throughput test (tokens/sec), and memory profiling. Results uploaded to model bench-results.
- Perf regression process: use nightly regression harness. Any change that causes a >5% degradation in p95 latency or throughput must trigger an ADR and rollback plan.

7) Decision records (ADRs)

Summary of canonical ADRs (examples):

- ADR-2025-01: Centralized API Gateway for auth, rate-limiting, and request routing. Owner: Platform. Rationale: single enforcement point for quotas and SSO.
- ADR-2025-07: Standardize on path versioning (/v1) for breaking changes. Owner: API team.
- ADR-2025-12: Adopt continuous batching in serving runtime with bounded-latency caps. Owner: Serving runtime.
- ADR-2026-02: Quantization profile taxonomy (A/B/C) and accuracy guardrails. Owner: Applied ML.

ADRs must include context, options considered, decision, and follow-ups. Add new ADRs for decisions that materially change behavior or operational burden. ADR template stored at /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records-template.

8) Operational playbooks and change procedures

Infra change process:

1. Submit Terraform PR with plan output and risk assessment.
2. Run smoke tests in staging and require two approvers for network/IAM/KMS changes.
3. Deploy during approved maintenance window unless emergency.

Model rollout playbook (summary - see model rollout runbook for full steps):

1. Prepare model package + bench results and register in model registry.
2. Canary 1% with synthetic tests for 24h.
3. Monitor: p95 latency, error rate, cache hit, quality metrics.
4. Ramp and validate at each step; abort on regression and run rollback.

9) Compliance & security notes

- Data residency labels must be included on APIs and model packages (e.g., eu-only).
- Audit logging required for model uploads, key usage, and access to private deployments.

10) Adoption & governance

- New services must include a short architecture checklist in their PR description referencing this document.
- Architecture review board (monthly) will review major ADR proposals, infra changes > $5k/month, and adoption of new quantization profiles.

Appendix B: Example OpenAPI snippet (schematic)

  paths:
    /v1/generate:
      post:
        summary: Generate text from a model
        requestBody:
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerateRequest'
        responses:
          '200':
            description: successful generation
          '429':
            description: rate limited
